title: Administrator
description:
Coffey, A Tetra Tech Company, is looking for a proactive Administrator to support the successful delivery of geotechnical engineering projects based in our Reading office.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

This is a pivotal coordination role, providing essential administrative, financial and operational support to project teams ensuring projects remain on schedule, compliant and efficiently managed. You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists and stakeholders to maintain project documentation, reporting, procurement activities, system administration and billing administration processes.

Your Impact in this Position

You will play a key role in keeping the office and projects running smoothly by ensuring accurate coordination, effective communication and strong administrative control across multiple workstreams. Your ability to manage competing priorities, maintain high attention to detail and support technical teams will directly contribute to successful project outcomes, improved efficiency and a positive client experience.

Core Capabilities

Project Coordination & Administration
- Deliver a professional, responsive support service to internal stakeholders and technical teams.
- Maintain schedules, trackers, reports and project documentation.
- Ensure records are accurate, organised and audit ready.

Communication & Stakeholder Support
- Coordinate meetings, workshops and project communications.
- Build effective working relationships across business and operational teams.
- Prepare and maintain accuracy across reports, presentations and project documentation.

Financial, Billing & Commercial Administration
- Lead on project system management, invoicing, billing administration and purchase orders. Support project budget tracking, timesheet coordination and cost reporting.
- Liaise with finance and wider business teams where appropriate.

Organisation & Time Management
- Organise travel arrangements to support project requirements including overseas.
- Manage multiple priorities across concurrent activities.
- Proactively follow up on actions and outstanding tasks.
- Maintain a structured and efficient approach in a dynamic environment. Technical & Systems Capability
- Use an Oracle based bespoke Tetralinx system for project finance management.
- Support reporting, document control and data management activities.

Training, Qualifications & Experience

Strong interpersonal and organisational skills are essential. Knowledge of integrated management systems and ISO accreditations would be beneficial. You should be confident using Microsoft 365 applications including Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint, with the ability to learn new systems quickly. Experience supporting engineering, construction, infrastructure or professional services teams would be highly regarded.

Working Environment

This is an office based position in our Reading office.

About Coffey, A Tetra Tech Company
Coffey is at the forefront of delivering design and feasibility solutions for engineering geology, geotechnical engineering, hydrogeology, and geo-environmental projects. The core of our business is geotechnical design consultancy including engineering geological, design for infrastructure projects (road and rail), water, energy, buildings and land developments.

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. We have a wide range of expertise across our teams, providing a global support network with a personalised approach to client relationships to better understand where we can add value. We provide a collaborative environment that supports individual performance, innovation, and creativity.

In alignment with the Equality Act 2010, we will make reasonable adjustments to support candidates and employees requiring additional arrangements. This could include adaptations to work schedules, training approaches, or the physical workspace. Please inform us if you need any accommodations during the recruitment process or in your day-to-day role.

title: Facilities & Operations Coordinator
company: PACT (Parents and Children Together) - Agency - Permanent
description:
Play a key role in supporting the workplaces, facilities and services that help us deliver our mission. Every day at PACT, we are building adoptive families and empowering women, children, and parents to embrace a positive future. Join an outstanding adoption charity and award winning trauma recovery service provider that is passionate about creating brighter futures for women, children and families for many different backgrounds.

Position: Facilities & Operations Coordinator

Location: Office based Reading, travel to other PACT locations as required

Contract: Permanent, full time 37 hours per week (Monday - Friday)

Starting salary range: £26,508 - £29,452 per annum

About the role:

As Facilities & Operations Coordinator, no two days will be the same.

Act as the day to day point of contact for facilities and workplace related matters

Help coordinate health and safety activities, building maintenance, contractor visits, office services and workplace arrangements and improvements

Ensure issues are identified, managed and resolved effectively

Work closely with internal and external stakeholders, building positive relationships to maintain environments that support the delivery of PACT's services

Coordinate repairs, support maintenance activities and oversee contractor works

Carry out inspections to ensure our buildings remain safe, compliant and maintained

Complete health and safety administration, monitoring and compliance activities

Assist with office improvement initiatives, premises projects and operational activities

Identify opportunities to improve workplace environments, processes and colleague experience

Our Facilities & Operations Coordinator role includes regular movement around our premises, including accessing all floors of our buildings, which do not have lift access. It also involves practical facilities duties such as receiving deliveries, moving supplies and carrying out workplace checks.

About you:

We're looking for a Facilities & Operations Coordinator who takes ownership, identifies issues and enjoys working with others to find practical solutions. You will enjoy keeping things organised, work collaboratively and be happy to get involved. Most importantly, you'll be proactive, practical and committed to delivering excellent support services.

You will also bring:

Experience of facilities, office management, operations or property-related administration, or similar

Experience of working with contractors, suppliers or external service providers

Adaptability to manage multiple priorities and respond to changing requirements

Good administrative and record keeping skills, with experience of Microsoft applications

Willingness to work independently, use initiative and maintain a positive, professional approach

Experience supporting health and safety activities, compliance processes or working within a charity, public sector or regulated environment would be advantageous. We recognise that relevant experience can be gained through a range of roles and environments, and we welcome applications from people whose experience may not match every competency.

If this sounds like you then visit our website and apply today to join a dedicated team who are part of something truly meaningful. We look forward to hearing from you!

Contact details to arrange an informal discussion about the role, will be found on our website.

Closing date: 5pm, Thursday 12 November 2026

Early applications are encouraged as we may review and appoint on an earlier basis if a successful candidate is secured.

Other roles you may have experience of could include:

Facilities Coordinator, Facilities Assistant, Workplace Coordinator, Office Manager, Office Coordinator, Operations Coordinator, Operations Assistant, Property Administrator, Facilities Administrator, Workplace Assistant, Estates Coordinator, Business Support Coordinator, Corporate Services Coordinator or Facilities Management Coordinator.

Safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do at PACT. We have robust measures and best practices in place to safeguard and protect the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults and we take pride in maintaining outstanding safeguarding standards. Anyone joining our team is subject to PACT's safer recruitment pre-appointment enquiries, including a Disclosure Barring Service (DBS). The role description provides information on what our safer recruitment enquiries include and the level of DBS required to work in the role.

All opportunities with PACT are based in the UK.

PACT is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and identities. We are committed to creating a working environment where everyone feels valued, respected and can contribute fully. We welcome applications from all candidates and are committed to considering reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process and employment

title: Receptionist
company: South Reading and Shinfield Group Medical Practice
advertiser_name: South Reading and Shinfield Group Medical Practice
description: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice reception team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Practice Manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Opening up/locking-up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system. Care Coordinator with strong administrative, organisational and communication skills. Processing personal, online and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail This is a 37.5 hours position (Flexible pattern), and will be during our opening hours 07:45-18:30 Monday to Friday. We also offer extended hours on a Saturday 08:00-12:00. The successful candidate will have and be able to demonstrate: Good customer service skills. Previous NHS GP Practice experience is desirable but not essential; Experience Care Coordinator with strong administrative, organisational and communication skills. Professional, approachable and friendly and efficient front-desk service; Experience of working in a team; Providing excellent customer service; Adept in using own initative when working alone; Experience working in a busy environment; The ability to multitask and prioritise effectively whilst staying calm under pressure; Has a good understanding of confidentiality; Flexibility in working pattern and duties; Ability to cope with and manage change; Computer literate. EmisWeb familiarity is desirable but training will be provided. Job responsibilities: Administration To have a thorough knowledge of all practice procedures To work in accordance of written protocols Pulling/filing notes for surgeries and updating as necessary Filing post in medical records Email and photocopy as requested Reception Receiving patients, consulting with members of practice team Handing completed repeat prescriptions to patient and checking names and address. Be able to cover all reception position as necessary Appointments Process appointment requests for today/future appointments from patients by telephone, email and in person. Deal with visits/requests Computer Process patients changes of address computer data and medical records (have knowledge of practice area) Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines Telephone Have working knowledge of telephone system, during and after hours Other Tasks Clear rooms after surgeries Ensure building security have thorough knowledge of doors/windows/alarm Any other tasks allocated by managers Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Demonstrate due regard for safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.
